title: Etale/pro-etale inverse-image square commutes with derived scalar comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $a:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of discrete commutative rings. Use constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and ordinary unbounded derived module categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $R=A,B$, $Z=X,Y$ and $t=e,p$ denoting the etale and pro-etale sites, write $C_Z^R=\nu_Z^*$ for comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $l_R=f_{\mathrm{et},R}^*$ and $p_R=f_{\mathrm{proet},R}^*$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $T_Z^t=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ for scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $d_R:p_RC_Y^R\xrightarrow{\sim}C_X^Rl_R$ be the canonical inverse-image square of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Let $c^e:l_BT_Y^e\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^el_A$ be the K-flat-normalized comparison [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso], and let $c^p:p_BT_Y^p\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^pp_A$ and $\delta_Z:T_Z^pC_Z^A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z^BT_Z^e$ be the canonical ringed pullback/scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Then, for every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\delta_{X,l_AM}\circ T_X^p(d_{A,M})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AM}=C_X^B(c^e_M)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eM}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,M}).$$
Both sides are morphisms $p_BT_Y^pC_Y^AM\to C_X^BT_X^el_AM$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, boundedness or flatness of $a$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, label lemma-derived-pullback-composition: ordinary module-pullback normalization, applied to the scalar/site cube

proof.text: Work first with ordinary module sheaves. Let $I=f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_Y^{-1}$ and $J=\nu_X^{-1}f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets, and let $\theta:I\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ be the specified geometric square. The first assertion of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives this square for every discrete coefficient ring, without its later qcqs hypothesis. Its module version $d_R^0$ is the lift of this same $\theta$, not a choice of unrelated isomorphisms for $A$ and $B$. Indeed [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] describes the coefficient lift by applying the inverse image to addition and scalar endomorphisms. Naturality with these operations makes $\theta$ additive and scalar-compatible. The components on constant ring sheaves identify their canonical pullbacks: for each $r\in R$, use naturality on $r:1\to\underline R$; the terminal-object component is the identity. These sections generate the constant sheaf by its sheafification definition [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. In particular $\theta_B$ respects $a$ relative to $\theta_A$, by naturality on $\underline a$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, underlying pullback square; ordinary square as specified in sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison

proof.text:
For an ordinary $A_Y$-module $N$, write $Q=B_Y\otimes_{A_Y}N$ and $q:B_Y\times N\to Q$ for the universal balanced pairing. Under the product identifications, $\theta_{B_Y\times N}=\theta_{B_Y}\times\theta_N$: composing with either projection gives this by naturality. Naturality on the pairing itself therefore gives
$$\theta_Q\circ I(q)=J(q)\circ(\theta_{B_Y}\times\theta_N).$$
Use the ordinary scalar/pullback maps normalized by scalar insertion and the generalized pure-tensor formula [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]; such a normalized comparison exists for the module pullbacks along $I$ and $J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction], applied to the $A_Y$-modules $B_Y$ and $N$ and composed with the constant-ring identification of Step 1. Identify $I(Q)$ with $B_X\otimes_{A_X}I(N)$ and $J(Q)$ with $B_X\otimes_{A_X}J(N)$ by these maps. Then the equation just written says that the route using $\theta_Q$ sends $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes\theta_N(m)$. The route first using scalar/pullback and then $B_X\otimes\theta_N$ has exactly that value. The coefficient is $b$ because Step 1 identifies $\theta_{B_Y}$ with the canonical constant-ring identification. The relation $ba(r)\otimes m=b\otimes rm$ goes to $ba(r)\otimes\theta_N(m)=b\otimes r\theta_N(m)$, so this is an equality of balanced maps. Pure tensors generate each presheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and its maps extend uniquely to its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Thus the two ordinary cube paths are equal as sheaf morphisms, including on generalized sections, not only on global constant sections.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: tensor represents balanced bilinear maps; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, canonical pairing

proof.text: Represent $M$ by a complex $K$ and choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and flat in every degree [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Regard every geometric inverse image, comparison inverse image, and coefficient extension as a ringed-topos pullback; for coefficient extension the underlying geometric morphism is the identity and the structural ring map is $a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], ordinary pullback preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms. Consequently every intermediate complex along either path, including $B\otimes_A P$ and its subsequent geometric pullbacks, is K-flat with flat terms over its current coefficient ring. The representative counits are isomorphisms and identify every iterated derived pullback with the ordinary iterated pullback of this one $P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. For the scalar edges this is also the K-flat computation in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Flatness here is a property of the resolving complexes; it imposes no flatness condition on $a$.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: Under the representative isomorphisms of Step 3, each of the SIX faces appearing in the requested equation has the ordinary normalization used in Steps 1--2. For $c^e$ this is precisely the defining representative-counit equation of [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso]. For $c^p$ and $\delta_X,\delta_Y$, use the specified ringed scalar/pullback comparisons: composition is computed by ordinary module pullback on flat-term K-flat complexes, and a specified compatible geometric 2-isomorphism induces the corresponding derived pullback isomorphism [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. This applies to the identity geometric morphism with structural map $a$ as well as to the geometric/site morphisms. For $d_A,d_B$, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] explicitly gives the same ordinary inverse-image square localized to the unbounded derived category, since all four fixed-coefficient inverse images are exact. Thus the ordinary cube equality of Step 2, applied degree by degree to $P$, localizes to the required equality at $\mathsf Q_A P$. No permutation of homogeneous factors occurs: the coefficient sheaf is in degree zero, and all maps commute with the differential by naturality in $P^n\to P^{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, proof on one common K-flat representative; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, representative normalization

proof.text:
Let $F=p_BT_Y^pC_Y^A$ and $G=C_X^BT_X^el_A$, and denote the displayed left and right paths by $\alpha,\beta:F\Rightarrow G$. All their factors are natural transformations by their definitions. For the isomorphism $u:\mathsf Q_AP\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ induced by the resolution, naturality gives $\alpha_M=G(u)\alpha_{\mathsf Q_AP}F(u)^{-1}$ and $\beta_M=G(u)\beta_{\mathsf Q_AP}F(u)^{-1}$. Step 4 makes the middle factors equal. This proves exactly
$$\delta_{X,l_AM}\circ T_X^p(d_{A,M})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AM}=C_X^B(c^e_M)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eM}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,M}).$$
Both paths start at $F(M)$ and end at $G(M)$, so no extra identification of their endpoints is being assumed. The resolution and pullback statements used above apply to arbitrary complexes on the fixed small sites; no geometric finiteness, boundedness, or coefficient-flatness hypothesis has entered.
